Public announcement

Public announcement

Four minutes of spoken word over a beat. It opens cold in 1976 and runs the record to the files still withheld, speaks to anyone working inside the institutions, and ends where it began. Free to download and play on repeat.

One pass · 4:13 · the beat drops out on the hard lines; the last line runs into the first

Playing it

  • Set the loop to repeat, or play the hour file straight through. Each pass is complete on its own, so anyone walking past hears all of it within a few minutes.
  • Check the local rules on amplified sound before playing it in public. Many cities limit volume and hours, or require a permit.
  • If you adapt the words, keep the lines to those inside: “This message does not ask you to disobey legal orders. It does not ask you to desert, to sabotage, to obstruct, or to leak.” Federal law, 18 U.S.C. § 2387, makes it a crime to urge members of the armed forces toward insubordination or refusal of duty. Those lines are what keep the announcement clear of it.

The words

Written down, filed

Nineteen seventy-six.

The Wall Street firm Bear Stearns checks his job application. He has written down a lecturing post at Berkeley. Its investigators find no record of it.

The firm keeps him, and makes him a limited partner.

Written down. Filed. And nothing changed.

The nineteen eighties. London. His own brother puts him there, in nineteen eighty-five.

A television investigation says that by the late eighties, he is in Ghislaine Maxwell's circle, while her father runs a media empire.

Nineteen ninety-six.

A young woman goes to the police in New York. She reports Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell.

She is sent on to the FBI.

Written down. Filed. And for ten years, nothing happens.

The deal

Two thousand and seven.

Federal prosecutors cut a deal. It grants immunity to people the government has not even named.

The Justice Department's own review will later call it poor judgment.

Thirteen months in a county jail. Out six days a week, on work release.

The open door

Then ten years as a registered sex offender. Public record. Anyone can look it up.

And heads of state, Nobel prize winners, cabinet officers, university presidents and the biggest banks in the country keep the door open.

JPMorgan flags him, and keeps him, until two thousand and thirteen.

The door stays open.

The cell

Two thousand and nineteen.

He is arrested, and charged with sex trafficking of minors.

Five weeks later he is dead. In federal custody. Before any trial.

No trial. No testimony. No cross-examination.

The dark

Ghislaine Maxwell is convicted. Twenty years.

The files? Some two hundred thousand pages, withheld or redacted.

New Mexico says federal prosecutors told it to stand down. It handed over its whole file. Ten more requests, ignored or denied.

The verse

Every one of those decisions had a person behind it. A signature. A desk.

Two thousand years ago, it was written of rulers who believed, and would not say so.

They loved the praise of men more than the praise of God.

To those inside

So this is for you. If you work inside a police force. A bank. A university. An agency. A uniform.

What that record documents has no hands of its own. It runs because trained people run it.

Your duty is to obey legal orders. Under military law, obeying a clearly illegal order is no defence.

This message does not ask you to disobey legal orders. It does not ask you to desert, to sabotage, to obstruct, or to leak.

If you see wrongdoing, go to an Inspector General, or a Member of Congress. For service members, federal law forbids reprisal for that: title ten, section ten thirty-four.

And do not send classified material to anyone.

Close

To everyone else: keep looking.

It is all written down. Dates. Documents. Sources. Every claim graded, every correction public.

Read it. Check one line. If it's wrong, prove it. If it's right, say it out loud.

The report is online. b0b.dev.

Spelled out. B as in bravo. Zero, the number. B as in bravo.

The report is online. b0b.dev.

This has been a public announcement, from a private citizen. It is not from the government, and it is not from the police.

Nineteen seventy-six. Nineteen ninety-six. Two thousand and seven. Written down. Filed. Nothing changed.

Not this time.

How it was made

The voice is synthetic: Piper’s en_GB-cori-high, a model trained on public-domain LibriVox recordings. The beat (kick, brushed snare, hats, bass and pad) is synthesised in the build script; nothing is sampled, and nothing in it is an alert tone, a siren or a lone sharp crack. Every fact in it is the report’s own, and no survivor is named. The address to anyone who serves is adapted from the report’s own, To those inside.

Before publishing, a speech-recognition model transcribed one pass as rendered and through four simulated street recordings: a small speaker at a distance, with traffic noise six, then three, decibels below the voice. In noise it got about 97% of the words right, and every sentence whose meaning rests on a negation (“does not ask you to disobey legal orders”, “do not send classified material”, “not from the police”) was heard with the negation intact, every time.
